newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end lower in sluggish session.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end lower in sluggish session.

text.p: Colombian stocks fell back slightly on markets that failed to shake off last week's sluggishness, brokers said.

Bogota's IBB index drifted down 0.16 percent to 867.84 on a 748.3 million peso volume. A wave of profit-taking in the country's three largest banks, Colombia, Bogota and Ganadero put downward pressure on the capital's exchange.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index suffered a marginal 0.09 percent loss, falling to 13,639.46 on a 572.5 million peso volume, on the back of drops in the value of Banco de Colombia and Banco Ganadero ordinary and preferential shares.

"Demand on the Bogota exchange never picked up and the market was depressed. The drop is mainly due to price speculation and in many cases by profit-taking on share portfolios. Given the low volumes traded, no trend is apparent. The only share that is still dynamic is (brewing giant) Bavaria because of expected good results," a Bogota broker said.

Banco de Colombia dropped back 0.95 percent to 416 on a total trade of 132.43 million pesos. The Banco de Bogota lost a wafer-thin 0.01 percent, falling to 6,050 on a volume of almost 49 million pesos. Banco Ganadero fell 0.73 percent to 270 on a thin 3.7 million peso trade.

"Demand from certain foreign funds and local investors, which usually gives a signal about the state of the market, never emerged and the markets stayed generally sluggish," another broker said. The only main share which gained was Bavaria, up 0.59 percent to 4,041 on a 268.5 million peso volume.

In Medellin, Banco de Colombia shares fell back 0.71 percent to 415 on a 2.5 million peso volume, while Banco Ganadero ordinary shares lost 0.92 percent, sliding to 270 on a 38.6 million peso total trade.
